Thanks, good questions. Attached is a concise test plan (Meridian_Perf_TestPlan_20270607.xlsx) and a short fallback matrix (fallback_matrix_v1.pdf). Summary below so you can ingest quickly:

- Baseline: run 15-minute steady-state at target QPS (you choose; typical production for customers of your size is 120 qps per endpoint).
- Spike profile: 10s ramp to 3x, hold for 5 minutes, then sustained 10x for 2 minutes, followed by 5-minute cooldown at 1x. We include an additional long-burst scenario: 30m at 2x to observe resource exhaustion patterns.
- Metrics we deliver: per-request latency (p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9), token-level emission timestamps, kernel-level GPU utilization traces (1s granularity), KV cache hit ratio time series, and request-level routing metadata (region, fallback used).
- Artifacts: aggregated CSVs and raw traces; sample load generator seed and request corpus used for the run.
- Graceful fallback: policy order is (1) local model-variant with lower memory footprint and quantization, (2) regional reroute to healthy pool (same model family), (3) degrade to single-token-chunk streaming mode to reduce memory pressure. Each action is instrumented and flagged in the per-request metadata so you can correlate latency jumps to fallback events.

I copied Vivek and Laura to add operational runbook details and confirm attachment availability.

—Markus
VP Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Priya —

Confirming the specifics you asked for and detailing the methodology we will run for the acceptance lab:

1) GPU traces and kernel versions
   - We will include per-GPU: memory utilization, allocation events (timestamped), CUDA kernel name mapping, and per-kernel execution latency. Kernel versions, driver versions, and BLAS/cuDNN/collective library versions will be documented in the run manifest.

2) KV-cache cold-start and eviction stress
   - We will run a synthetic workload that simulates prefix locality degradation: episodic namespace churn where 80% of requests hit a 20% prefix set, then we shift distribution to new prefixes over a 10-minute window to force eviction. Output: cache hit ratio, miss latency contribution, and charted warmup time (time to 90% of steady-state hit rate). See attached kv_cache_simulation_agg.csv for a sample of the simulation output from a previous run.

3) Tail-latency decomposition and root-cause tagging
   - For each tail event (>p99.5) we will provide a tag: fallback-triggered, cold-kv-miss, preemption-schedule, packing-delay, or model-variant-swap. Each request in the delivered CSV will have a small set of metadata fields (request_id, event_tag, route, model_variant).

4) Acceptance lab and reproducibility
   - We propose a 3-hour on-site remote lab window where Redwood runs the agreed scenarios and streams the live metrics. After the run we will ship a reproducible artifact bundle: load generator commands, request corpus, seed, Docker image hashes, and the raw metrics.

Operational notes:
- We recommend your team run a parallel lightweight traffic mirror to observe client-side TCP and TLS behavior. Server-side traces will be comprehensive, but a client mirror helps correlate end-to-end latencies.
- If you want a more conservative spike (less risk to production), change the 10x sustained burst to 5x sustained for the long-burst scenario.

I'll attach the sample CSV and matrix in the email thread. Laura — can you add the suggested lab window options and an SLA-related acceptance criterion draft (e.g., acceptable p99.9 delta thresholds)?

Thanks,
Vivek
Principal, Applied Performance — Redwood Inference

Draft acceptance criteria for your review (we'll adapt based on your compliance needs):
- p50/p90/p95: within 10% of control-run baseline
- p99: no more than 1.5x control-run baseline during short spikes (<=5m)
- p99.9: no systemic uplift >2.0x; any single-host preemption events must be documented and excluded from a systemic failure call if they are scheduled maintenance or known cloud interference
- Tail-cause attribution: >=95% of tail events must have an assigned event_tag in the delivered CSV.

- Option A: Wed 2027-06-16 08:00–11:00
